note: Status as reported by NASA, ESA, JAXA and press sources listed per mission, checked on the as_of date. Positions: landers from NASA Mars Trek waypoints (HiRISE-located) or NASA/JPL rover feeds; future landing regions are IAU gazetteer centres, not final ellipses.

missions.name: Viking 1 lander
missions.science: First successful Mars landing; biology experiments; 6 years of weather.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Viking orbiter colour mosaic (MDIM 2.1) is the colour base map of the globe.
missions.for_crews: The first surface weather record; the soil chemistry crews will handle.

missions.name: Viking 2 lander
missions.science: Seasonal frost on the surface; second biology test site.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Heritage site in Landing mode.
missions.for_crews: Seen frost at mid-latitude: ice is near.

missions.name: Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner
missions.science: First rover; airbag landing on an outflow-flood plain strewn with rocks.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Heritage site.
missions.for_crews: A rock-strewn flood plain: what a boulder field looks like up close.

missions.name: Spirit (MER-A)
missions.science: Hot-spring silica at Home Plate; volcanic rocks of Gusev.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Traverse and science stops on the globe (Mars Trek).
missions.for_crews: Lost in soft soil at Troy in 2009, ground that looked firm from orbit: why MarsNav prices soft soil by its worst outcomes.

missions.name: Opportunity (MER-B)
missions.science: Hematite spherules and sulfates from ancient acidic water; 45 km to Endeavour crater.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Traverse and science stops on the globe (Mars Trek).
missions.for_crews: Ended by the 2018 global dust storm (solar power): the dust-storm scenario in the planner.

missions.name: Phoenix
missions.science: Dug into water ice a few centimetres down; found perchlorate salts.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Heritage site; ice layers (SWIM, GRS).
missions.for_crews: Shallow ice is real, and so is perchlorate, a toxicity hazard for crews and suits.

missions.name: Curiosity (Mars Science Laboratory)
missions.science: A habitable ancient lake; since 2025 the boxwork ridges of Mount Sharp, left by groundwater; 47+ drill samples.
missions.data_in_marsnav: RAD surface radiation dose (EVA dose and the cosmic-ray map); the Mount Sharp boxwork EVA site; the traverse to its latest sol; raw camera images.
missions.for_crews: The only long radiation record on the surface; the boxwork site is the challenge's own example.

missions.name: InSight
missions.science: Marsquakes and the size of the core and crust; the heat-probe mole stalled in cohesive soil.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Heritage site; the gravity map shows the crust InSight probed.
missions.for_crews: Soil can be stronger than expected too: dig tools must cope with duricrust.

missions.name: Perseverance (Mars 2020)
missions.science: River delta and lake of Jezero; cored samples including Cheyava Falls, a potential biosignature (2024).
missions.data_in_marsnav: MEDA weather (the climate model), the traverse, real sample sites as EVA stations, the validation case study, raw camera images.
missions.for_crews: The planner's flagship EVA site; terrain-relative navigation landed it inside a hazard field.

missions.name: Ingenuity helicopter

site.name: Jezero crater
site.note: deployed near the Perseverance landing site

missions.science: First powered flight on another planet: 72 flights, scouting routes for the rover.
missions.for_crews: Aerial scouting ahead of a traverse is proven.

missions.name: Tianwen-1 Zhurong rover
missions.science: Ground-penetrating radar of buried layers in southern Utopia; hibernated in May 2022 and did not wake.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Heritage site.
missions.for_crews: Dust on solar panels ends missions: the dust-cover layer matters.

missions.name: Mars 3
missions.science: First soft landing on Mars; signal lost after about 20 seconds.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Heritage site.

missions.name: Beagle 2

site.name: Isidis Planitia
site.note: found intact by HiRISE in 2015; its panels did not all open

missions.for_crews: One stuck deployment ends a mission: why checklists and procedures live in the app.

missions.name: Schiaparelli (ExoMars 2016 EDM)
missions.for_crews: Entry, descent and landing are where missions are lost; the landing ellipse is part of the dossier.

missions.name: Mars Global Surveyor
missions.science: MOLA laser altimetry, TES thermal spectroscopy, magnetic field.
missions.data_in_marsnav: MOLA elevation (the datum of every map), MOLA roughness, TES thermal inertia, albedo, minerals and dust index, gravity tracking.

missions.name: 2001 Mars Odyssey
missions.status: active (reported operating in July 2026; propellant nearly used up)
missions.science: THEMIS infrared; GRS gamma-ray and neutron spectrometers; relay for the rovers.
missions.data_in_marsnav: THEMIS day / night infrared base maps; GRS water, iron, chlorine, potassium, thorium, silicon; chloride deposits.
missions.for_crews: Relay link: fewer relay orbiters means fewer contact windows for a crew.

missions.name: Mars Express
missions.science: HRSC stereo camera, OMEGA mineral spectrometer, MARSIS radar.
missions.data_in_marsnav: HRSC + MOLA blended elevation (200 m) and colour relief; OMEGA hydrous-mineral detections.

missions.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
missions.science: HiRISE (25 cm), CTX (6 m), CRISM, SHARAD radar, Mars Climate Sounder; main relay.
missions.data_in_marsnav: HiRISE and CTX elevation models and images (every EVA site), CRISM mineral detections, recurring slope lineae and new craters, GMM-3 gravity, gullies, glaciers.
missions.for_crews: Almost every hazard the planner sees comes from MRO.

missions.name: MAVEN
missions.science: Upper atmosphere, solar wind and atmospheric escape; also a relay.
missions.for_crews: Contact lost on 6 December 2025; NASA ended the mission in mid-2026. One fewer relay and no upper-atmosphere space-weather monitor at Mars.

missions.name: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
missions.science: Trace gases (methane search), FREND neutron map of near-surface water, CaSSIS colour stereo; relay.
missions.for_crews: Relay for Perseverance and Curiosity.

missions.name: Emirates Mars Mission (Hope)
missions.science: Whole-planet weather and dust every few hours from a high orbit.
missions.for_crews: The kind of synoptic weather picture a crew would want each morning.

missions.name: Tianwen-1 orbiter
missions.science: MoRIC global mosaic, high-resolution camera, subsurface radar.

missions.name: Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)
missions.science: Colour imaging and atmosphere.

missions.name: ESCAPADE (two spacecraft)
missions.science: Two small orbiters measuring the solar wind and Mars' magnetic environment at the same time.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Will give the space-weather picture at Mars itself that crews need for radiation forecasts (DONKI today predicts arrivals from Earth-side data).
missions.for_crews: Launched on New Glenn on 13 November 2025, waiting near Earth-Sun L2 to leave for Mars in late 2026; arrival planned for autumn 2027.

missions.name: Martian Moons eXploration (MMX)
missions.science: Phobos samples (at least 10 g) back to Earth in 2031; the IDEFIX rover on Phobos.
missions.for_crews: Phobos is a candidate staging point for human missions.

missions.name: Mars Telecommunications Orbiter
missions.years: delivery by end of 2028; operational by 2030
missions.science: High-rate relay network for Mars.
missions.for_crews: Replaces the ageing relay fleet (MAVEN lost, Odyssey near its end): more contact time for surface crews. NASA selected Blue Origin on 1 September 2026.

missions.name: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover

site.name: Oxia Planum
site.note: IAU centre of Oxia Planum; the landing ellipse lies in the plain

missions.science: A 2 m drill for organics below the radiation-damaged surface, in clay-rich ancient rock.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Oxia Planum's clays appear in the aqueous-mineral layer.
missions.for_crews: Tells crews how deep they must dig for intact organic molecules.

missions.name: Tianwen-3 sample return
missions.years: launch ~2028 (may slip to ~2030); samples to Earth ~2031
missions.science: First Mars samples to Earth; 86 candidate sites studied, mostly in Utopia and Chryse.
missions.data_in_marsnav: Candidate regions on the globe.

missions.name: Mars Sample Return (NASA / ESA)

site.name: Perseverance sample tubes, Jezero
site.note: region only: the tubes are in Jezero crater

missions.science: Perseverance's cored samples were to be brought to Earth; the FY2026 budget left the retrieval unfunded.
missions.data_in_marsnav: The sample sites are the Jezero EVA stations.
missions.for_crews: A human crew may be the one that brings the Jezero samples home.

missions.name: SpaceX Starship to Mars (uncrewed)
missions.science: Cargo landers ahead of crews.
missions.data_in_marsnav: The 7 Starship candidate sites (Golombek et al. 2021) and the Starship criteria in Landing mode.
missions.for_crews: In February 2026 SpaceX moved its near-term focus to the Moon; first Mars landings would follow later.

missions.name: First crewed landing
missions.science: Human field science: the reason MarsNav exists.
missions.data_in_marsnav: 48 NASA Exploration Zones (2015) screened against the human landing-site criteria; the EVA planner.
